assign.outcome:
**Local whisper is running, and the owner's voice becomes text on screen while they talk.** whisper.cpp (cuBLAS b5130) + `large-v3-turbo` installed outside the repo at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lew42\whisper\`, running on the RTX 4070 SUPER's CUDA0 -- a 10-second clip transcribes in 76-98ms, about 1% of real time. `whisper-server` is left running (`http://127.0.0.1:8178`, PID in the task log) with open CORS, so the browser talks to it directly -- no dev-server change needed.

A new module, [`ux/Dictate`](/framework/ux/Dictate/), replaces the old silent `ext/Ask/mic.js` button: a mic with four visible states (idle, listening, transcribing, error), a real level meter, live GREY partial text every ~1.5s while whisper is still guessing (the owner's own complaint -- 'it's not transcribing in real time' -- answered directly), a `Ctrl+Shift+M` shortcut named in the button's tooltip and its own status line, and an opt-in 'stop after a pause' checkbox with a visible, cancellable 2.5s countdown (off by default -- ending a dictation stays an explicit button press or shortcut, never a silent auto-submit). Falls back to the browser's own `SpeechRecognition` when whisper is not running, and draws no button at all when neither engine is reachable. `ext/Ask/reply.js`'s reply mic AND its big dictate box both build on this now, through the single `acts()` method they share -- `ext/AITask/asks.js:126`'s call site did not need to change.

Proven headless with a fake microphone (Playwright + `--use-file-for-fake-audio-capture`) on a private `:8134` server: a synthesized JFK sentence became text in the textarea with a 356ms latency from the stop press to the text landing; the send_on_pause countdown auto-stopped correctly against a genuine 4s silence clip; whisper-down and neither-engine fallbacks both behaved exactly as designed. Eight screenshots at 1280 and 400 are in `shots/`.

**Left for later, with why:** who starts `whisper-server` automatically -- three options written down in `doc/decisions.md`, none built (the leading one touches `Server/**`, owned right now by the sibling `server-self` task); the level-meter and silence thresholds are reasonable starting numbers, not calibrated against a real microphone; `mic.js` is kept (not deleted) since nothing else in the repo imports it and the brief asked only to fix its wrong privacy claim.
